cross_product_finding: Two distinct findings on this page. (1) Same access-model mismatch as createindex.json: Prerequisites keys the privilege off 'cluster access credential type,' not privilege:query-manage-index. (2) A genuinely new pattern for this batch: the ALTER INDEX WITH clause's 'action' property has a 'move' value and a 'nodes' property that are explicitly, unconditionally disabled on Capella ('You cannot use this action in Couchbase Capella, as it defaults to file-based index rebalancing' / 'You cannot use this property in Couchbase Capella...'), reinforced by an error-message row: '"nodes" clause is disabled with alter index as file based rebalance (shard affinity) is enabled.' This is structurally identical to the requiresEdition/behavesDifferentlyUnder pattern used for Enterprise-vs-Community differences on server/ - a specific clause/option is available in one context and not another - except the axis here is Capella-vs-self-managed-Server (i.e. product/deployment), not edition. I minted deployment:capella as the object concept and reused the behavesDifferentlyUnder predicate, since inventing a whole new predicate seemed unnecessary when the relation shape already matches; only the concept vocabulary for 'what varies' needed to be extended. This is a strong candidate for the coordinator to consider whether 'edition' in the registry should be generalized to a broader 'variant/deployment axis' concept, since Capella clearly has its own analogous axis of feature availability even though it has no Enterprise/Community split.
